purpose: De-risk T0.3 over a longer baseline: does the 25.8% hold, and does the answer difference compound?

config.note: 20 root steps from RD0016 cycle 2110 to 2130, both arms concurrent on separate nodes. Dumps landed every root step (21 each) - the CycleSkipDataDump=5 override did not gate because make_bench_run.py strips CycleLastDataDump from the restart deck. Unplanned, but it gave a per-step divergence trace, which is better for the question.

timing.verdict: HOLDS. 24.8% at 20 steps vs 25.8% at 5 steps - the 1-point difference is inside the ~1.6% node scatter, and the barrier reduction reproduces (62.0->47.2% at 5 steps, 63.9->49.5% at 20). The short-run result was not an artifact of the one-time restart-layout transition.

divergence_trend.columns: root step | baryon rel | dm rel | stellar rel | stars(control) | stars(512) | delta stars %
divergence_trend.conservation: Impeccable. Dark matter stays at machine precision (1e-15/1e-16) with no trend; baryon mass 1e-9. Nothing leaks.
divergence_trend.star_deficit: SYSTEMATIC and LINEAR. The 512 arm forms fewer stars at every checkpoint - the sign never flips, so this is not chaotic divergence. Rate is constant at 0.015/0.017/0.018/0.016 % per root step, reaching 0.334% (4816 stars) by step 20. That is ~1000x the identical-code noise floor (+-1 star).

OPEN_ISSUE: See audit/status.yml T0.3 note and ROADMAP.md section 5.5 - the star deficit is an unresolved follow-up, NOT a blocker for short runs but unquantified for long campaigns.
recommendation: The speedup is real and durable. Do NOT adopt for a long production campaign on the speedup alone until the star deficit is understood: naive linear extrapolation gives ~1.7% at 100 root steps and ~8% at 500, but 20 steps is far too short to know whether it saturates. Short runs and testing are unaffected.
